extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and practitioners preparing or prosecuting nonprovisional international (Hague) design applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination, form & content, and prosecution of nonprovisional international design applications (Hague Agreement) designating the United States, including inventorship, applicant identity, title/description/claim, reproductions, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication by the International Bureau (Hague Art. 10(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The international registration shall be published by the International Bureau; such publication is deemed sufficient publicity in all Contracting Parties and the International Bureau shall send a copy of the publication to each designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication by the IB is treated as the operative publication for all designated Contracting Parties; no other publicity may be required of the holder. The USPTO will systematically receive published international registrations designating the United States pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 10(3) and examine them in due course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of International Registration as National Application (Hague Art. 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the date of the international registration, the international registration shall have at least the same effect in each designated Contracting Party as a regularly-filed application for protection of the industrial design under that Contracting Party's law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An international registration designating the United States acts, from its registration date, as the equivalent of a U.S. application for purposes of examination and prosecution under applicable U.S. law (subject to any refusals under Article 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to Refuse by Designated Offices (Hague Art. 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated Office may refuse the effects, in part or whole, of an international registration in its territory where the conditions for the grant of protection under that country's law are not met, but may not refuse on grounds that requirements relating to form or contents provided for in this Act or the Regulations or additional to them have not been satisfied under the law of the Contracting Party concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusals must be substantive (e.g., failure to meet national protection conditions) and cannot be based solely on form/content differences that are covered by the Hague Act/Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of U.S. Application File upon Article 10(3) Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the publication under Article 10(3), the USPTO will establish an application file for examination; if the Office was the office of indirect filing, that application file will be used and retain the same application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will send a filing receipt indicating U.S. application number, U.S. filing date, inventorship, applicant, and other bibliographic data. The U.S. application file will be made available to the public via Patent Center after Article 10(3) publication; prior access is governed by 37 CFR 1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: National/Nonprovisional Application Treatment (37 CFR 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.9(a)(1) and (a)(3), the terms 'national application' and 'nonprovisional application' include an international design application filed under the Hague Agreement in which the Office has received a copy of the international registration pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such international design applications are treated as U.S. national/nonprovisional applications for rule applicability and prosecution purposes and are sometimes referred to as 'nonprovisional international design applications.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for International Design Applications (37 CFR 1.41(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of an international design application designating the United States is the creator(s) set forth in the publication of the international registration under Hague Agreement Article 10(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any correction of inventorship must follow 37 CFR 1.48 (see MPEP §602.01(c) et seq.). Inventorship corrections require a corrected ADS identifying legal names, residence, mailing address (37 CFR 1.76(b)(1)), and the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)). Changes after Office action on the merits require an additional fee (37 CFR 1.17(d)). A required executed oath/declaration or substitute statement (37 CFR 1.63/1.64) must be provided for any added inventor who has not executed one (37 CFR 1.48(b)). When an inventor is improperly identified as a juristic entity (illegal under U.S. law), use Form Paragraph 29.04 to reject the claim under 35 U.S.C. 171 and 115 and instruct correction via 37 CFR 1.48(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Juristic Entity as Inventor (U.S. law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under U.S. national law, the inventor cannot be a juristic entity even if foreign law allows it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a nonprovisional international design application identifies a juristic entity as an inventor, the examiner should reject the claim and use Form Paragraph 29.04. Applicant must correct inventorship via 37 CFR 1.48(a) and submit a properly signed and marked-up ADS plus required fees and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Inventorship — Content & Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48(a) must identify the inventorship change and be accompanied by a corrected application data sheet (ADS) including the legal name, residence, and mailing address of each actual inventor and the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)); the ADS must identify changes with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for deletions (37 CFR 1.76(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed after the Office action on the merits, the request must also include the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(d). A required oath/declaration or substitute statement will be required for any actual inventor who has not executed one (37 CFR 1.48(b)). MPEP §602.01(c) provides detailed discussion and sample language/form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Identity and Changes (37 CFR 1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person (assignee, person to whom inventor obligated to assign, or person showing proprietary interest) identified as applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(b) must have been identified as the applicant in the publication of the international registration under Hague Agreement Article 10(3); a 37 CFR 1.46 applicant identified as the applicant in the publication is the applicant in the nonprovisional international design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to the applicant after filing require a corrected ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the applicant and must comply with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73. The new applicant must establish ownership under 37 CFR 3.71(b) and 3.73. A name change recorded under Hague Article 16(1)(ii) may also effect the change in the U.S. application if recorded no later than payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence Address Priority (37 CFR 1.1066)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless changed under 37 CFR 1.33(a), the Office will use as the correspondence address in a nonprovisional international design application, in order: (1) the correspondence address under 37 CFR 1.1042; (2) the address of applicant’s representative identified in the publication of the international registration; (3) the address of the applicant identified in the publication of the international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to the correspondence address set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(a) shall be construed to include this section for nonprovisional international design applications. See MPEP §601.03(a) for further info about changing correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title Requirements (37 CFR 1.1067)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the design must designate the particular article in which the design is embodied; the title must correspond to the article named in the claim, and the title may not be directed to less than the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may provide a title via an ADS (37 CFR 1.76) or by amending the specification (37 CFR 1.121). If applicant does not supply a title, the Office will establish one by retrieving the first listed product indication on the published international registration (INID code 54). When the article named in the title and the article named in the claim do not correspond, the examiner should object under 37 CFR 1.1067 and require correction (use Form Paragraph 29.59.02 or other form paragraphs as appropriate). When the applicant furnished the title, applicant approval is required for examiner's amendment to the title; when the Office established the title, applicant approval is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of Title Throughout Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the language of the title should be made at each occurrence of the title language throughout the application, except in the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article named in the title is not present in the original figure descriptions, it is not necessary to incorporate the article into the figure descriptions as part of an amendment to the title. Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 15.05.01, 29.59.01, 29.59.02) with bracketed instructions to effect title amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification — Minimal Description Required (37 CFR 1.1067)
rubrics_metrics.description: No description other than a reference to the drawing is ordinarily required in a nonprovisional international design application; the drawing is ordinarily 'its own best description.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a written description is not required, it is not prohibited; if provided, figure descriptions must clearly and accurately describe views (e.g., 'front view,' 'perspective view'). Examiners should object to unclear or inaccurate descriptions and suggest corrective language (Form ¶29.60.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'Reference View' Terminology in Figure Descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are cautioned against using 'reference view' as a figure description in international design applications designating the United States because that term has no special meaning in U.S. practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'reference view' will be treated as another view of the design and any inconsistencies between it and other figures may cause uncertainty as to claim scope, potentially leading to rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) as nonenabling and indefinite. Describing a reference view as not included in the claimed design may still cause uncertainty if it includes features shown in other views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible and Prohibited Statements in Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements permissible in design applications under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16 (e.g., indicating nature & environmental use of design, purpose of broken lines) are permissible in nonprovisional international design applications; the specification may not include statements describing matters directed to function or unrelated to the design or suggest other embodiments not illustrated (except mirror images or obvious variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements that attempt to broaden the scope of the claimed design beyond what is shown are not permitted. Applicants may include statements explaining that protection is not sought for certain features; when excluding portions, applicants are strongly encouraged to indicate them by broken lines (or coloring) and include a statement explaining the meaning of broken lines/coloring (see MPEP §2920.05(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken Lines and Coloring — Identification & Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When protection is not sought for portions shown in a reproduction, applicants are strongly encouraged to indicate such matter by broken lines (or coloring) and include a specification statement explaining the meaning of the broken lines (or coloring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP provides model Examiner's Amendment form paragraphs for adding descriptions of broken lines (¶29.22), broken lines as boundaries (¶29.24), and coloring (¶29.26). These form paragraphs include bracketed fields for the structure/type and the appropriate explanatory wording. Applicant authorization is required for certain Examiner's Amendments; guidance in each form paragraph indicates when applicant authorization and preceding form paragraphs are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color Drawings/Photographs — Handling and Form Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains at least one color drawing or photograph, the examiner should not require the applicant to amend the specification to reference the color drawing/photograph; the examiner may add a statement using a form paragraph identifying that the patent contains at least one color drawing/photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form ¶29.61.01 may be used in an Examiner's Amendment to add a statement that copies with color drawings/photographs will be provided upon request and payment of a fee. This form paragraph is for international design applications and applicant authorization is not required for this Examiner's Amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Form & Content — Single Claim Requirement (37 CFR 1.1025)
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent application may include only a single claim. The specific wording of the claim in an international design application designating the United States shall be in formal terms to the ornamental design for the article (specifying name of article) 'as shown' or 'as shown and described.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification includes a proper descriptive statement or showing of modified forms of the design, the words 'and described' must be added to the claim. Unless amended by applicant, the examiner should not object as to matters of form but should amend the claim by Examiner's Amendment to include 'and described' where appropriate. Use form paragraphs 15.62, 15.63, 15.64 to amend claim wording as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions (Drawing Figures) — Must Be Complete and Clear (37 CFR 1.1026; Hague Rule 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every design application must include a reproduction (drawing in black & white or color, or photograph) of the claimed design; because the drawing/photograph constitutes the entire visual disclosure of the claim, it must be a clear and complete depiction of the design applied to the article and nothing regarding the design sought to be patented should be left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements for reproductions are set forth in Hague Agreement Rule 9 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions. The USPTO may object to amended reproductions that fail to comply with these formal requirements (use Form ¶29.10). Drawing requirements in 37 CFR 1.84 generally do not apply, except as set forth in 37 CFR 1.84(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure Numbering for International Registrations (Administrative Instruction 405)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the same industrial design is represented from different angles, numbering shall consist of two separate figures separated by a dot (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 for the first design, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 for the second design, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The figure numbering appearing in the published international registration should be preserved during prosecution before the USPTO. If designs are cancelled (e.g., due to restriction), applicants should not renumber the figures of the remaining designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to Amended Reproductions that Fail Formal Requirements (Form ¶29.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Form Paragraph 29.10 to object to amended reproductions received that do not comply with the formal requirements of Rule 9 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the date the amended reproductions were received and the reason for the objection (e.g., 'the reproductions are not of a quality permitting all the details of the industrial design to be clearly distinguished' or 'the reproductions contain explanatory text or legends'). Do not use this form to object to reproductions that were contained in the international registration published by the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification Objection for Missing Figure Descriptions (Form ¶29.60.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is objectionable under 37 CFR 1.1067 for failing to provide figure descriptions; the description should indicate the type of view shown in each figure (e.g., 'front view,' 'perspective view,' 'top view').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some but not all figure descriptions are missing, the examiner should indicate which descriptions are missing (identify figure numbers). Use Form ¶29.60.02 to make this objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on Statements Describing Function or Other Embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification of a nonprovisional international design application is not permitted to include statements describing matters that are directed to function or are unrelated to the design; the specification may also not include statements that describe or suggest other embodiments of the claimed design not illustrated in the drawing disclosure (except mirror images or shapes evident from the one shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such prohibited statements may nevertheless be included in the original filing to provide antecedent basis for a future amendment, but applicants should not include statements that attempt to broaden the claimed design beyond what is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of Published Bibliographic & Figure Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Information (e.g., figure numbering, applicant/creator) in the published international registration should be preserved during prosecution; the Office will generally retain the same application number when acting as office of indirect filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for international registration number using Patent Center. Prior to publication, access is governed by 37 CFR 1.14. Use published data to establish the U.S. filing receipt and bibliographic details.
